# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

# A connection is pointed at another schema while a sheet is shown as of a date (asof/); the pool
# puts it back on PUBLIC when it is returned.
spring.datasource.hikari.schema=PUBLIC

spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa

# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

    person_id BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    amount    DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    created   BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,

);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

Rollover undo is in, but **`bin/e2e` does not fully pass: 3 of the 4 tests pass and "rollover undo scenario 1" still fails.**

**Why scenario 1 fails:** at spec line 610, `wes` (who has the viewer role) generates periods for 2026-01 to 2026-02, and the test expects a count of `0`. The app already refuses every change from a viewer and shows `period-generate-error`, so the helper gets `null`. The expected audit for that test shows nothing written by `wes`, so the refusal itself matches. But I can't see how any implementation would show "0" there without breaking the rule that a refused action shows its error. This step has nothing to do with rollover, so I left it alone. Tell me if you want that behaviour changed.

**What I built**
- **Storage:** a new migration `V98__sheet_rollover.sql` keeps each sheet's last rollover: the fiscal year, who made it, the sheet-today it was made on, the periods it generated and the opening balances it set.
- **Server:** `POST /api/sheets/{id}/rollover-undo` (`UndoRollover.java`) removes the generated periods, takes back the opening balances and writes `ROLLOVER_UNDONE sheet=… by=… fy=FY2026`. It refuses, writing nothing, when:
  - there is no rollover left to undo,
  - the user isn't the steward who made the rollover,
  - the sheet-today has changed since, or
  - any claim, including a voided one, falls in a generated period.
- **Front end:** a `rollover-undo` button next to Roll over. A refusal shows the existing `rollover-error`.

**Two other changes the spec needed**
- **Rolling over the same year again no longer sets opening balances a second time.** If a rollover makes no new first period, it now sets none (the test expects `periods=0` with no `OPENING_SET` lines). Before this, the second rollover doubled Ada's opening balance to 3.00 where the test expects 2.00.
- **Refused pastes were leaving claims behind (scenario 3).** This app's repositories use JdbcTemplate directly. The `govern: [ transaction ]` setting only applies to Spring Data repositories, so it never actually opened a transaction. Each write was saved as it happened, and a paste refused partway through kept its earlier lines. I wrapped `PasteClaims` in its own transaction, and I checked through the API that a refused paste now writes nothing. **The same problem probably affects other endpoints** that write several things and can then be refused. I only fixed the paste because it was the one the spec hit.
